experiment.question: What is the Core doing at its ceiling: 14,250 devices at 50 to 100 ms per PDU, max-repetitions 5, 300 threads, the rung that failed?
experiment.plan: Hold the failing rung of the 300-thread search and capture Core and Minion for seven cycles with every live collector (JFR, GC logs, perf, procfs, pcap, the metrics topic), then describe the state before the Core is resized to 32 GiB with a 20 GiB heap. Nothing is changed during the window.

jvm.flags: JAVA_HEAP_SIZE=10240, JAVA_INITIAL_HEAP_SIZE=8192, -XX:+UseG1GC, -XX:NativeMemoryTracking=summary, MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=4 (systemd drop-in), Prometheus JMX exporter on 9299.

One change against the pool-200 search. Everything else is identical.

PostgreSQL, unchanged

host.cpu: 2 x Intel Xeon E5-2650 v4 @ 2.20 GHz, 24 physical cores / 48 threads; 28 vCPU running across 6 VMs
host.disk: ZFS pool scummbar, 808 GiB, SATA SSD

workload.generator_scenario: nl6 v0.28.0, cisco_crs_x.json, 144 interfaces per device, SNMP v2c, 10.42.0.0/16 one /24 per 250 devices; uniform 50-100 ms per-packet delay injected on the simulator bridge; GETBULK max-repetitions 5 for the fleet range

figures.title: Collections completed per second against the rate the fleet requires
figures.note: Required is the daemon's own collectable service count divided by the 300 s interval. Achieved sits below it for the whole window: the collector cannot keep up and the gap is what the queue accumulates.

figures.title: Collectd pending queue, rolling one-minute peak and floor
figures.note: The floor never touches zero: this is the runaway the 300-thread search stopped at, seven cycles of it.

figures.title: Collectd thread pool occupancy against its 300-thread ceiling
figures.note: JMX gauge from Collectd. At this fleet the pool is at its ceiling in every sample: collections take longer under a starved processor, so 300 slots are never enough, and the queue below never drains.

figures.title: CPU busy: Core, Minion and database
One-minute load per vCPU, every collection VM
figures.note: Normalised by vCPU count so a 2-vCPU broker and an 8-vCPU Core read on one scale. Above 1.0 means runnable work is queuing.

figures.title: Core JVM heap against its ceiling, and old-generation collections
figures.note: Heap between 8 and 10 GiB against the 10 GiB ceiling, old-generation collections at 2.3 a minute. This is the ceiling the cleanroom report named at 14,000 devices with 0.1 ms agents, reached here with 50 to 100 ms agents, max-repetitions 5 and 300 threads.

figures.title: SNMP on the simulator bridge: Minion enp6s20 and netsim enp6s19
figures.note: The same wire seen from both ends. The two lines should coincide; where they do, nothing is lost on the bridge.

series.label: minion enp6s20, SNMP to the fleet
netsim enp6s19, SNMP from the fleet

figures.title: Kafka segment: Minion RPC responses and Core producer
figures.note: The RPC responses the Minion returns to Kafka outweigh the SNMP that produced them. Transport costs more than telemetry.

figures.title: Database connection pool on Core during collection
figures.note: Read from the client side, since no PostgreSQL exporter runs in this lab. Metrics never touch PostgreSQL under exclusive Kafka forwarding; what the pool carries is Collectd scheduling state, the self-monitoring JDBC collections and provisiond.

figures.title: CPU busy: Kafka broker and network simulator

answers.question: What does the failing rung look like over seven cycles?
Which resource is the ceiling: processor, heap, pool, or something downstream?
How many metrics does the ceiling deliver?
Is anything else in the lab near a limit?
What the resize is expected to change

gaps.question: Was this a steady failing state or still degrading?
gaps.why: The fleet had been at 14,250 since 02:43 UTC, five hours before the window. The queue floor and the old-generation rate are read across the window to say whether they were still moving.

gaps.question: Is the CPU share collection or GC?
gaps.why: Both rise together; the GC log and JFR in the capture separate them, and this report reads the JMX collection-time counters, not the JFR.

gaps.question: Does the failure mode transfer to a real fleet?
gaps.why: 14,250 simulated devices with identical MIB trees; a real fleet's tables vary in size and the per-collection cost with them.

gaps.question: Would a larger heap alone move the ceiling, or does CPU bind first?
gaps.why: At 90% CPU and 22% of wall time in GC the two are entangled; the resize to 32 GiB / 20 GiB heap that follows this capture is the experiment that separates them.
